However, using any named source, having feedback scattered across those sources, and needing automated capture are not established; the email appropriately says to start with a supported source rather than claiming I already use one. Whether this fits my current workflow remains unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I am responsible for product work at a software company.
Email-only: My team receives useful feedback through Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Gong, or Zoom.
Email-only: Reviewing conversations, tickets, or reviews separately creates enough work to justify automation.
Email-only: Automatically deduplicating requests and routing them to teams would fit my product-review process.
reads.problem_now: Converting individual customer comments into reviewable product requests is plausibly important for my role, but the profile does not establish that I currently use a supported source, lose requests across channels, or need to solve this now.
reads.biggest_doubt: I cannot judge whether the extraction, duplicate merging, and team triage are accurate enough to trust, and the proposed test requires connecting a customer-data source before the email shows what I would be able to inspect or correct.
reads.to_click_it_would_have_to: I could test the extraction on a sample conversation or ticket before connecting a live customer-data source.
fixes: Rewrite "Once connected, it automatically captures feedback from customer chats, sales calls and reviews." to clarify what access the connection requires and whether I can test with sample data first.

Rewrite "The resulting feedback appears in Canny, where Autopilot triages it to the right team." to explain whether I review or correct extracted requests, duplicate merges, and routing before they affect the team workflow.

Replace "Create your Free account, choose a supported source and see how its feedback is captured, deduplicated and triaged." with a smaller, concrete first step that states whether source connection is required immediately.
reads.persona:
Selected audience (explicit constraints): Product manager or product team lead at a software company.
The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (inferred; applicability must be checked): People responsible for product decisions at software companies pull customer feedback from multiple channels (sales/CS calls recorded in tools like Gong, support tickets, Slack) into a central place such as a feedback portal or ProductBoard so requests can be reviewed by the product team rather than lost across departments.
Source: https://visioneers.gong.io/configuring-gong-76/can-i-use-gong-to-capture-product-feedback-and-connect-that-to-a-slack-channel-145; quote: In addition, we’re using our [ProductBoard integration](https://integrations.gong.io/integrations/productboard) to send highlights to ProductBoard, where our Product team reviews suggestions and feedback.
Source: https://craft.io/blog/product-feedback-management/; quote: It connects the voice of the customer to the product backlog, to prioritization decisions, and ultimately to what ships on the roadmap.
Problem context: A link to an entire call recording is not a usable unit of feedback downstream; practitioners want the specific moment or comment isolated and routed, not the whole call, and existing tooling lacks a way to auto-route by fine-grained tag/hashtag into separate channels. [Source limits: Publication date unknown; retrieval today does not establish current applicability.; Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://visioneers.gong.io/configuring-gong-76/can-i-use-gong-to-capture-product-feedback-and-connect-that-to-a-slack-channel-145

selected_brief.selection_reason: Product teams need feedback in a form they can review and act on. Extracting individual feature requests from conversations directly addresses the documented problem with passing around whole-call links, while the Free plan supplies a concrete introductory step.

value_case.reader_benefit: If customer feedback arrives through support or sales conversations, the product team can work from extracted, deduplicated requests that have been triaged instead of relying on whole-call links as the feedback unit.
value_case.mechanism: Autopilot reads call transcripts, support tickets and reviews, pulls out feature requests, merges duplicates and triages feedback to the appropriate team.
decision_conditions: The Free plan is $0 per month billed yearly and includes 25 tracked users.
Named sources such as Gong and Intercom are examples, not assumed parts of the recipient's stack.
Do not imply that Autopilot provides fine-grained hashtag routing into separate Slack channels.

claim_conditions: If the Free offer is described, retain both $0 per month billed yearly and the 25-tracked-user scope.
Autopilot is included in all plans, but do not imply zero setup effort or compatibility with an unconfirmed workflow.
Describe Gong, Intercom or other sources conditionally unless the recipient's installed stack is known.

Do not promise: Replacing or removing the incumbent Gong-to-ProductBoard and hashtag routing setup
Do not promise: Any time saved or hours recovered (Hive's 2-3 hours/week is one customer's self-report, not a promise)
Do not promise: Zero disruption, no setup effort, or no added headcount
Do not promise: Routing feedback into separate hashtag-based Slack channels or buckets
Do not promise: MCP server access, which requires a paid plan
Do not promise: Ranking or weighting requests by account revenue/ARR on this free path (the $10K-vs-$500K example is a customer's own prioritization outcome, not a Free/Autopilot feature)
